answer: One concrete mechanism: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because tide only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. In practice haven is enforced by the ledger itself: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
